pr_title: ESQL: Infer not null for aggregated fields
pr_body:
Since the majority of aggregations discard null values, filter them to
 begin with.
 | STATS x = min(a), y = sum(b) BY c
 becomes
 | WHERE a IS NOT NULL OR b IS NOT NULL
 | STATS x = min(a), y = sum(b) BY c

Fix #102787

issue_context.title: ESQL: Imply `IS NOT NULL` constraints for some aggs/functions/operators
issue_context.body:
### Description

Most aggs push ignore `null` values. In this example:
```
FROM logs-postgres*
| DISSECT message \"duration: %{query_duration} ms\"
| EVAL query_duration_num = TO_DOUBLE(query_duration)
| STATS avg_duration = AVG(query_duration_num)
```

comments:
Went after this one and implemented in #103030 only to discover that we cannot just apply the filter since it will end up the empty groups.
Consider the following entries with columns a and b
[1, x]
[2, null]

The query `stats count(a) by b` becomes `where a is not null | stats count(a) by b` which filters out group `2` as it has only null values.
This could be a dynamic filter that gets applied after discovering the set of groups (filter by filter) which makes it much less valueable.

review_comments: Why not break when the first match is encountered?

If you could add one more test with two aggregations that show how the `bool` query looks like, that would be great.
For example `from test | stats agg_emp = sum(emp_no), min_s = min(salary)` where the push down should look something like `{"bool":{"should":[{"exists":{"field":"emp_no"}},{"exists":{"field":"salary"}}]}}`
This could be made more generic with a List of Tuples or similar, likely we'll use it for some other rules in the future. But can be made like that when the need arises.
I think this needs a grouping.
It doesn't. The filter only gets added if no grouping is present since it can filter them out if all the group values are null.
